problems.detail: Stage 4: 5 workplaces, 100 teams, 2,000 staff, 36 months, 3,600 rosters. Attempted 5,523,066 bytes (~5.5MB). Failed at sfshift_apps: "Failed to execute 'setItem' on 'Storage': Setting the value of 'sfshift_apps' exceeded the quota." localStorage then held base+units+drafts+notifications but NOT apps or company.
problems.fix: Persist must warn the user when a save fails instead of silently continuing; the app should not keep running on unsaved state. Consider chunked storage / IndexedDB for large companies.

problems.message: Company data LOST — company rosters dropped from 3,600 to 720 (workplaces 5 → 1) after viewing a calendar while over quota
problems.detail: Stage 4 final state: companyWorkplaces 1, companyRosters 720, apps 0 (was 1,600). Chain: renderCalendar → resolveCalRoster → findSavedRoster → loadSaved → companyLoad → S.company = null (sfshift_company never persisted due to quota) → companyEnsure() rebuilt a company with only the active workplace. Then loadShiftApps pruned pending apps for the vanished workplaces.
problems.fix: companyLoad must not null S.company when storage is empty AND S.company already has workplaces; findSavedRoster must not call loadSaved unconditionally; persist must warn on quota failure instead of silently continuing.

problems.message: Company Stats compute took 11,580ms at 2,000 staff — break threshold crossed (>10s) (measured AFTER the wipe, over 720 rosters, not the full 3,600)
problems.detail: Stage 4 Stats measured after the company wipe, over the wiped 1-workplace company = 720 rosters (not the full 3,600). 720 rosters → ~11.6s matches Stage 2's 600 rosters → 11.6s. True Stats time at 3,600 rosters would be far higher.
problems.fix: Stats recomputes over every roster on every view — cache per-workplace aggregates, compute incrementally, or paginate the Stats view.
